headline: Tech stocks surge on both sides of the Pacific, but a looming RBA rate hike next week is the big story for everyday Aussies.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Strong day for the AI ETF, closing up 2.76% on the ASX. The broader AI sector got a boost from positive sentiment around Alphabet's Gemini 3.8 and a strong tech session on Wall Street last night. Still down about 9.25% overall from what you've put in — but today's move is a step in the right direction.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO popped 2.18% last night, likely riding the GTA 6 hype wave. Rockstar Games updated its modding guidelines ahead of GTA 6's release, keeping the game in the headlines. Still sitting about 9.6% below your average buy-in — the long-term thesis here is all about GTA 6 delivering.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG rose 1.88% last night after analysts lifted earnings estimates and strong Q2 2026 figures kept the stock near record levels. The launch of Google Gemini 3.8 is also putting Alphabet's enterprise AI revenue story front and centre. Up 14.1% on your investment.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft gained 1.59% last night as part of a broad tech rally on the NASDAQ, which surged 2.26%. No specific news catalyst — just the market continuing to reward big AI-exposed tech names. Up 13.2% on your investment.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS closed up 1.13% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's strong US market session. This ETF tracks the entire US sharemarket, so when Wall Street has a big night, VTS usually follows. Up 3.89% overall on your investment.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE nudged up 0.84% today — a solid quiet session. Emerging markets have been reasonably steady, and the AUD/USD holding around 71 cents isn't creating much drag. Just slightly in the green on your overall investment.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG ticked up 0.71% today — a calm, steady session for this diversified fund. It holds a broad mix of global and Aussie shares, so it tends to move smoothly. Essentially flat on your total investment, which is to be expected for a fund you've just started building.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS went exactly nowhere today, closing flat at $4.13. Lithium carbonate prices continue to trend weakly globally, with analysts pointing to multiple bearish factors converging — oversupply and soft demand from China being the key culprits. PLS is down 38.7% on your investment, the biggest drag in your portfolio right now.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike next week — now locked in by all four big banks
watch_today.detail: CBA and ANZ have both flipped their forecasts and now expect the RBA to raise interest rates at next Tuesday's board meeting, joining NAB and Westpac. CBA has already hiked its fixed mortgage rates ahead of the decision. RBA Governor's speech this week reportedly sealed the deal. A rate rise means higher mortgage costs for Aussies — and it could put some pressure on growth stocks and the broader ASX in the short term. Keep an eye on this.

watch_today.title: Hold PLS.AX — lithium pain continues but selling now locks in a big loss
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals closed flat today and is down nearly 39% on your investment. Lithium prices globally are still under pressure from oversupply and weak Chinese demand. There's no quick fix here. But selling now crystallises the loss — the long-term case for lithium in the energy transition is still intact, it's just taking much longer to play out than the market expected. Sit tight unless your conviction in the thesis has genuinely changed.

watch_today.title: Hold GXAI.AX — AI ETF bouncing, still below your buy price
watch_today.detail: GXAI closed up 2.76% today — a strong session — but you're still about 9.25% below your total invested amount. The AI sector is getting real positive tailwinds from Gemini 3.8, strong Google and Microsoft results, and growing enterprise AI revenue. No reason to bail; this is a long-term structural story. Hold and let it run.

watch_today.title: Hold TTWO — GTA 6 is the whole thesis, and it's still coming
watch_today.detail: Take-Two rose 2.18% last night and Rockstar updating its modding guidelines ahead of GTA 6 is keeping the hype alive. You're still about 9.6% below your buy-in price overall, but the entire bull case for TTWO rests on GTA 6 being a monster release. Nothing's changed there. Hold and wait for the launch catalyst.

watch_today.title: Middle East conflict escalating — watch oil and global market risk
watch_today.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards have threatened to 'change the geography of war' if the US escalates further, and Trump has threatened to 'obliterate' Iran. Despite this, oil actually fell 2.84% last night to USD $93 — markets may be pricing in some diplomatic circuit-breakers. But if things deteriorate sharply, oil could spike, inflation fears could return, and that's bad news for rate-sensitive stocks and your portfolio broadly. One to watch this week.

watch_today.title: GOOG and MSFT both up solidly last night — long-term holders in good shape
watch_today.detail: GOOG rose 1.88% and MSFT rose 1.59% last night, both near record levels with analysts raising earnings forecasts. You're up 14% on GOOG and 13% on MSFT. No action needed — these are exactly the kind of long-term compounders you want to hold. Enjoy the ride.

world.summary: The Middle East conflict is rapidly escalating with the US and Iran trading threats, global leaders are wrestling with how to regulate AI, and the US midterm elections are 40 days away with Trump leaning heavily on Biden as his campaign target.

stories.title: Middle East war: Iran threatens to 'change geography of war' as US warns of rapid escalation
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's Revolutionary Guards have publicly warned they will 'change the geography of war' if the US escalates its involvement in the Middle East conflict. Trump has threatened to 'obliterate' Iran in response. The US has separately warned allies of the risk of rapid, uncontrolled escalation. Saudi Arabia, which recently signed a new defence pact, is now caught in the middle and faces a major test of that agreement. For everyday people, this conflict risks pushing oil prices up sharply, which flows through to petrol prices and inflation worldwide.

stories.title: US midterm elections are 40 days away — and Trump's campaign is all about Biden
stories.why_it_matters: US midterm elections are now just 40 days away, and Trump has mentioned Joe Biden nearly 900 times on the campaign trail — making him the central villain of his pitch to voters rather than focusing on his own record. Analysts warn Trump risks looking backward rather than governing, and could face an early 'lame duck' period if Republicans underperform. The midterms will determine whether Trump retains control of Congress, which matters enormously for US economic policy, tax and spending — all of which flow through to global markets.

stories.title: OECD September 2026 Economic Outlook: global growth holding but risks rising
stories.why_it_matters: The OECD has released its September 2026 global economic outlook, with global growth and inflation forecasts in focus. While the headline numbers suggest global growth is holding up, the report flags rising risks — particularly from Middle East conflict pushing energy prices higher, and persistent inflation in some economies. For Australia, a weaker global economy would hit export demand, especially for resources like iron ore and lithium.

stories.title: 13-year-old Yu Zidi wins record-breaking swimming gold, calls it 'so-so'
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi, just 13 years old, has won a record-breaking gold medal at a major international swimming event — making her one of the youngest ever to win a major at that level. When asked about her performance, she simply shrugged and called it 'so-so.' The story has gone viral globally as a charming moment of understated brilliance from a teenager who seems utterly unfazed by her own history-making achievement.

politics.summary: All four big banks now expect the RBA to raise interest rates next week — a significant shift that will directly affect Australian mortgage holders and investors alike.

stories.title: All big four banks now tipping RBA rate rise next Tuesday
stories.why_it_matters: CBA and ANZ reversed their previous forecasts and are now tipping an RBA interest rate rise at next Tuesday's board meeting, joining NAB and Westpac. That means all four of Australia's biggest banks are aligned. The RBA Governor's final speech before the meeting reportedly sealed the deal, cementing bets among traders and economists. CBA has already hiked its fixed mortgage rates ahead of the official decision. If you have a variable-rate mortgage, this means your repayments are about to go up again.

stories.title: CBA lifts fixed mortgage rates ahead of expected RBA move
stories.why_it_matters: CBA has already moved to hike its fixed-rate home loans ahead of the RBA decision, becoming the last of the big four to do so. This is a pre-emptive move — banks don't wait for the RBA to actually act before adjusting fixed rates, since those are priced off market expectations. If you're on a fixed rate coming up for renewal, expect to be rolling onto a higher rate. Variable rate holders will feel it the moment the RBA pulls the trigger next Tuesday.

ai.summary: A major antitrust lawsuit has been filed against the world's biggest AI companies, accusing them of secretly agreeing to slow down AI development — while separately, Australia and dozens of world leaders are pushing for tougher global AI regulation.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI hit with antitrust lawsuit over alleged AI slowdown pact
stories.why_it_matters: A landmark antitrust lawsuit — a legal challenge to anti-competitive behaviour — has been filed against OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Elon Musk's xAI (SpaceX AI). The claim alleges the companies secretly agreed to pump the brakes on AI development to protect their dominant market positions, rather than for genuine safety reasons. Critics call it a carve-up of the AI market dressed up as responsible development. If proven, this could be one of the biggest antitrust cases in tech history and could fundamentally reshape the AI industry.

stories.title: Australia joins global push for tougher AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Australia has formally backed an international push for tougher AI regulation, citing 'risk to safety and security'. Dozens of world leaders are listening to warnings from tech giants about AI's risks, and there are now serious global conversations about what a regulatory framework — similar to how we regulate medicines or aviation — could look like for AI. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GOOG and GXAI, heavier regulation could constrain some growth, but also adds legitimacy to the sector long-term.

stories.title: Google Gemini 3.8 Live puts Alphabet's enterprise AI revenue in the spotlight
stories.why_it_matters: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Live — a real-time, conversational AI model designed to compete directly in the enterprise (business) AI market against Microsoft's Copilot. Analysts are watching closely to see whether Alphabet can translate its AI capabilities into actual recurring revenue from businesses. Strong Q2 2026 results have already lifted earnings estimates, and the stock is near record highs. For GOOG holders, this is the core of why the investment thesis remains strong.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 3 teams are announced with big news on the Roosters and Panthers, while the AFL Grand Final is approaching with a Brisbane Lion redemption story in focus.

stories.title: Roosters make huge Walker call; Penrith name Cleary — NRL Prelim Finals teams revealed
stories.why_it_matters: The Roosters have made a major selection call on Walker — reports suggest it's history-making for the NRL — while Penrith have made what's described as an 'obvious' decision to name Cleary for their preliminary final. The Dolphins host the Roosters on Friday night at Suncorp Stadium (7:50pm), and the Panthers take on the Knights on Sunday at Accor Stadium (4:00pm). Big week of footy ahead for Gold Coast fans — Suncorp is just up the road.

stories.title: Fox Sports pundits back Knights to upset Panthers in preliminary final
stories.why_it_matters: Despite Penrith being heavy favourites, Fox Sports pundits are arguing the Knights can cause a shock upset in Sunday's preliminary final. The Knights have surprised throughout the finals series and belief in their camp is high. If they win, it would be one of the biggest upsets in recent NRL finals history.

stories.title: AFL Grand Final approaching — Brisbane Lion's redemption story after heartbreak
stories.why_it_matters: With the AFL Grand Final around the corner, AFL.com.au is profiling a Brisbane Lions player whose journey back to the big stage was driven by the pain of a previous Grand Final heartbreak. The Lions are described as a 'selfless' unit with genuine Grand Final ambitions. The government is also warning fans to watch out for ticket scalping ahead of the big day.

markets.summary: Last night was a big one on Wall Street — the NASDAQ surged 2.26% and the S&P 500 gained 1.49%, with tech stocks leading the charge. The ASX had a quieter but positive day, up 0.30%. Oil dropped sharply despite Middle East tensions, and gold eased slightly. The Aussie dollar is sitting around 71 cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Quiet positive session today — the ASX followed Wall Street's lead but with much more modest gains.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Strong session last night — broad-based gains across most sectors, with tech leading the way.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Big night on the NASDAQ last night — the tech-heavy index surged over 2%, driven by Alphabet, Microsoft and AI-sector momentum.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell nearly 3% last night despite escalating Middle East tensions — markets may be betting on diplomatic de-escalation, or supply concerns are being offset by demand worries.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold eased slightly — a minor pullback after a strong run. Still at historically elevated levels.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar is basically flat — holding around 71 cents. A potential RBA rate rise next week could give it a small boost.
